newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco representatives firm on immunity - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco representatives firm on immunity - WSJ.

text.p: Tobacco industry representatives said they would consider altering the proposed $368.5 billion settlement with the states in a way that would change provisions granting the industry immunity from punitive damages for past conduct, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Friday's electronic edition, the newspaper said two industry delegates, speaking on condition of anonymity, said they would consider altering parts of the accord governing the Food and Drug Administration's ability to regulate nicotine content in cigarettes and the penalties tobacco companies must pay if youth smoking does not decline.
But they drew the line at immunity for past misdeeds.
One of the industry delegrates said "flatly" that he did not see any way cigarette makers could give up immunity from punitive liability in civil lawsuits based on past conduct, the report said.
